findings.impact: Calling harness will receive a validation error (TypeError: agy_run_observe() got an unexpected keyword argument 'run_id') when executing the suggested next tool after a progress stall, causing the harness to crash/fail.
findings.message: terminal_observe_call constructs a ToolCall with the argument 'run_id', but the registered MCP tool agy_run_observe in server.py expects 'run_ids' (a list of strings). This mismatch makes the suggested tool call invalid. tests/test_supervision.py asserts this incorrect contract at lines 449-452.

findings.impact: Stale/cleared attention events are matched and returned by wait_for_runs when condition='any_attention', waking up the calling harness prematurely with stale needs_attention events and causing potential wedges/loops.
findings.message: _matching_events filters on ATTENTION_EVENTS, but attention suppression/clearing events (mcp_input_submitted, mcp_input_delivered, attention_cleared) are not in ATTENTION_EVENTS. Consequently, they are filtered out, and wait_for_runs can match and return older needs_attention events even after they have been resolved. No tests cover this suppression behavior inside wait_for_runs.

findings.impact: Fragility in cursor tracking if the run ID key in run_dirs does not match the physical run directory name.
findings.message: _next_after matches run_id from event.get('run_id') (which is run_dir.name) against run_ids keys of run_dirs. If they do not match, the cursor sequence updates are silently skipped.
